title: I made a roguelike deckbuilder with AI-assisted art: what worked, what didn’t
author: BigSlickNick2
selftext:
I’ve been building Breathless Crown, a roguelike deckbuilder you can play in your browser. You’re a salvager aboard a dying king’s ark, and the main twist is oxygen: moving, fighting and some cards cost air, and if it runs out the run ends. The ark also orbits a dying sun, so cards play a Sunlit or a Shadow face depending on the phase.

What’s in it right now

* Two classes: the Salvager Knight, who chains Parry → Thrust → Cut into combos, and the Eclipse Huntress, who sets moths on enemies and bites with them in the dark
* Four decks to climb, each with its own Champions and warden, and the Hollow King at the top
* Parts you pull from wrecks and bolt onto cards, in 15 sets with bonuses at 2, 3 and 4 parts
* A full run takes about 30–40 minutes

How the art was made  
Card art, characters and backgrounds were generated with Scenario, then cropped, cleaned up and fitted into a set of rules I kept for the style.

What worked

* Writing down a short style guide early (palette, lighting, what never appears) and reusing it in every prompt kept a few hundred images looking like one game.
* Painted backgrounds plus code-drawn effects (lightning, hit sparks, shield bubbles) made it feel alive without needing animated sprites.

What didn’t

* Consistency between characters is still the hardest part. Some enemies came out facing the wrong way and had to be redone.
* AI art can make a game look finished before it plays like one. Most of my time has gone into balance, not art.

What I’d like feedback on  
Gameplay, fairness, fun, art, I would love your opinions on the game. 

Playtest build, in your browser: [https://bigslicknick.itch.io/breathless-crown](https://bigslicknick.itch.io/breathless-crown)

comments.author: Minimum_Scholar_8136
comments.body:
Let me commend you on your achievement here. I am myself working on vibe coding a game in a similar genre. I particularly liked the writing of the intro, your original concepts for the sword technique, the development of your protagonist.

  
The pulsating effect on your enemies is pretty well done - my AI was just recommending something similar to me.

replies.author: BigSlickNick2
replies.body: Thank you! Anything you noticed bad or recommendations?

comments.author: Ludophiliac
comments.body:
Well, let's start from this looking very much "gen AI". Not saying because it is gen AI, it just looks the way people don't want game art to look like when its made out of AI. It needs some art direction. Think of games with praised art and try to understand what makes them unique. I know it is rather hard to do with AI but that's what's going to separate you from the vibe-developers in terms of art.

Also there is the issue with lacking game design. A game needs to be designed in such a way to ease the player into liking the game, learning how to have fun from the game. These kinds of game design stuff are more important than ever because technically making a game is easy nowadays. I can't say do this, do that for this game because this is an expertise, a profession of game design which requires a lot of thinking and growing a mindset. I don't know how well you know these kinds of stuff, but I can say from playing 5 minutes of this game, there is very little thought that went into this when making this game.

Sure this looks and plays better than a greybox prototype but don't get caught up thinking that you can make a great game by vibing your way through. Try to decompile Slay the Spire, as that is your main reference. Try to understand the decisions that went behind making the game what it is. Also look into what they changed, into the second game. What needed to be improved, cut from the game? 

I know thinking and learning with pre-historic ways (less AI 😂 ) might be lower dopamine than just vibing your way through a game, but I think it is very very beneficial.

replies.author: BigSlickNick2
replies.body: Hey thanks for the advice. Art has always been my weakness, so thats where I always needed the most help, so with direction it was a theme and certain things to not have and have and kinda went from there. As far as design goes, all this is a mixture of a hobby,passion project, and learning as I go, and hope that anything I pick up along the way could make things better.

replies.author: Ludophiliac
replies.body: No worries. I understand that not everyone is a professional and an expert when making a game but I believe that AI can help less experienced people get into making games, which is great. What I would advise you would be to make smaller games. Designing and balancing a Slay the Spire-like (if thats a word, lol) is very very challenging to say the least. And that would not teach you as much as making a small game where you can grasp the design and think about it yourself, rather than riding the AI all the way.

replies.author: BigSlickNick2
replies.body: In my head I thought these type of games would be easier to make in comparison to most lol.

replies.author: Ludophiliac
replies.body: Well, yes but no. Easier to make games are harder to design.
